about.title: San Diego Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: San Diego County is home to a large network of hospitals, surgical centers, urgent care clinics and specialty practices serving well over a million residents in the city alone. Most visits go the way they should. Sometimes they do not, and when a provider falls short of the accepted standard of care, California law gives the injured patient a path forward. That path is narrower than many people expect. Under MICRA, a claim generally must be filed within one year of discovering the harm and never more than three years after the injury itself. A 90-day notice must go to each provider before suit is filed. Non-economic damages are capped, though the cap rises annually. And a bad outcome by itself is not malpractice; a qualified medical expert almost always has to explain what should have happened differently. We are a medical malpractice law team that handles these cases on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why San Diego Patients Choose Us

items.title: The clock is shorter than you think
items.desc: MICRA gives you roughly one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury. Getting started early protects that window.

items.title: Notice and expert requirements are handled for you
items.desc: California requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to each provider, and a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to establish what the standard of care demanded. Our team knows how to line both up.

items.title: Honest answers about what a claim can and cannot recover
items.desc: Non-economic damages in California malpractice cases are capped by statute, though the cap rises each year. You get a straight explanation of how that applies to your situation, not a sales pitch.

items.question: My surgery had a complication. Does that mean I have a malpractice case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor result on its own is not malpractice; there has to be a departure from the accepted standard of care that caused the harm. That usually requires a qualified medical expert to review the records and say what a reasonable provider would have done differently. We can arrange that review and tell you frankly whether the facts support a claim.

items.question: I was treated at a military or VA facility in San Diego. Are the rules different?
items.answer: Often, yes. Claims involving federal facilities, which are common in the San Diego area, generally proceed under federal procedures with their own notice requirements and deadlines, rather than the state MICRA framework alone. Sorting out which rules apply is one of the first things we will do, so it helps to mention where you were treated when you reach out.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to a malpractice attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle medical malpractice cases on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
